name: Teaching at the Right Level Africa (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The locations the sheet's bottom line reads (row labels naming Zambia, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire), sharing equally.

missing_data.note: Measured: TaRL Africa counts the pupils reached in each country, and the learning gain is from randomised trials of Teaching at the Right Level, including government-run delivery (India, Ghana, Zambia), halved for fidelity at scale.

summary: TaRL Africa helps governments in Zambia, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire and other countries regroup primary pupils by learning level for daily reading and maths sessions. The Life You Can Save estimates 3.57 learning-adjusted years of schooling per $100 from TaRL Africa's 2024 costs, the governments' costs and pupils reached, with half the trials' learning gain kept at scale. Our view turns the learning gain into later earnings with the site's shared figure; the biggest uncertainties are how much of a childhood test gain lasts into adult earnings and how much of the learning the governments would have achieved without TaRL Africa.

sections.title: The Life You Can Save's bottom line
From learning-adjusted years back to learning gains
sections.explainer: charityevals' step. Learning-adjusted years of schooling have no shared conversion to the site's scale; the site values learning by the later earnings a gain in test scores brings. So the sheet's figures are turned back into standard deviations of learning per dollar, and the three countries pooled by their money.

source.title: The Life You Can Save, TaRL Africa cost-effectiveness estimates (sheet '2025')
source.quote: RCTs in India and multiple African countries (e.g., Ghana, Kenya, Zambia) show that TaRL can increase foundational learning by 0.15 to 0.7 standard deviations

rows.explainer: The Life You Can Save takes the bottom of the range the trials of Teaching at the Right Level found (Banerjee et al. 2016 and 2017 in India; Lipovsek et al. 2023), 0.15 to 0.7 standard deviations in reading and maths depending on how it is delivered. Range from the same note: 0.15 to 0.7 (its spread across trials, not a confidence interval). Kept as the best guess in our view too: the smaller gains in those trials came where the government's own teachers ran the sessions in school hours (Haryana, in Banerjee et al. 2017), the delivery TaRL Africa supports; the large ones came from intensive camps run by Pratham's staff and volunteers. The fidelity step below is a separate question, how much of a supervised trial's effect survives when a ministry runs it in every school.

rows.label: Share of the trials' effect kept at scale (fidelity)

source.title: The Life You Can Save, TaRL Africa cost-effectiveness estimates (sheet '2025')
source.quote: We apply a subjective 50% discount rate to account for the likely decrease in effectiveness of this intervention when scaled outside of experimental, controlled settings

rows.explainer: The sheet calls it a 'discount rate', but it is not a discount for time: it halves the trials' effect because programmes run at scale by governments are delivered less faithfully. The Life You Can Save takes the middle of the 23% to 83% fidelity Angrist and Meager (2023) found across studies (https://edworkingpapers.com/sites/default/files/ai23-802.pdf); that range is the range here.

rows.label: Learning gained per dollar, the three countries pooled by their money (pupil-SD per $)
rows.formula: (sd_per_dollar_zambia * total_cost_zambia + sd_per_dollar_nigeria * total_cost_nigeria + sd_per_dollar_cote_divoire * total_cost_cote_divoire) / total_cost_core
rows.explainer: Our step: the three countries weighted by the money spent in each, so the figure is what the average dollar did across them; the sheet takes the plain average of the three countries' ratios, which counts Zambia's cheap pupils as much as Côte d'Ivoire's dear ones. Pooled, the learning-adjusted years come to 3.13 per $100 rather than 3.57.

rows.label: TaRL Africa's spending outside the three countries' expenses, per dollar of them
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 20% (5% to 40%). The sheet's costs are 'Core Country Expenses Only (2024)': the three country programmes. A dollar given to TaRL Africa also pays its central team (training, measurement, fundraising, management) and its lighter support to the other countries it works with, and the sheet counts no learning from those either, so we add the central part as a cost. Anchor: TaRL Africa's budget is 12.1 million dollars for 2025/26 (The Life You Can Save's recommendation page, https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/best-charities/teaching-at-the-right-level-africa/) against 3.6 million spent in the three countries in 2024; most of the difference is other countries' programmes and growth, which we take to do about as well as the core countries, and the rest central costs. TaRL Africa's own accounts with that split aren't public.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of TaRL Africa's spending
rows.explainer: The shared default for technical assistance and policy work (@staff_pay.share_research_policy): TaRL Africa's spending is mostly its own staff training and coaching government trainers and officials. We haven't seen its breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared default for advisers and policy staff (@staff_pay.gap_research_policy).

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of TaRL Africa's spending (in-kind donation)
rows.explainer: Staff's pay below market as a share of what TaRL Africa pays: counted as a cost only with credit by share of resources on.

rows.label: Full cost per dollar of the sheet's costs
rows.formula: (total_cost_core + nonprofit_cost_core * (1 + if($resource_shares, salary_sacrifice, 0)) * (1 + central_cost_share) - nonprofit_cost_core) / total_cost_core
rows.explainer: The sheet's costs plus TaRL Africa's central costs (above) and, with credit by share of resources on, its staff's forgone pay, over the sheet's costs. The governments' money is counted here as the sheet counts it; the bottom line then takes it out of the cost (adopter_cost_out) and nets it from the good. Off (the default) this is about 1.07.

rows.label: Learning gained per dollar, all costs counted (pupil-SD per $)
rows.explainer: The pooled learning per dollar over the full cost.

rows.label: Pupils reached per dollar
rows.explainer: The learning per dollar over the learning per pupil (0.075 SD): about one pupil for every 6 dollars of all the programme's money.

rows.label: Adult earnings gain per standard deviation of skill still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for low- and middle-income countries (@education.earnings_gain_per_sd_adult_skills_lmic: 20%, 10% to 30%), from the Center for Global Development's review of the studies linking adults' reading and maths to their earnings, per SD of skill still there in adult life.

rows.label: Share of the pupils' learning gain still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (@education.test_gain_persistence_to_adulthood: {{row:learning_persistence}}, 20% to 70%): test-score gains fade, a fifth to a half of a year's learning carrying into the next grade in Pakistan's schools (Andrabi and others 2011). No study yet follows Teaching at the Right Level's pupils into work.

rows.label: Adult earnings gain per standard deviation of a childhood learning gain
rows.explainer: 20% per SD of adult skill × 40% of the gain lasting = {{row:earnings_gain_per_sd}} higher earnings per SD of a childhood learning gain. The Life You Can Save stops at learning-adjusted years and puts no value on them.

rows.label: Gain in ln(earnings) per pupil, each working year
rows.explainer: 0.075 SD × 8% = 0.6% higher earnings, as a change in log consumption.

rows.label: Years from the programme to adult earnings
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 9 years (6 to 12): Teaching at the Right Level sessions are for pupils in grades 3 to 5, about 9 to 11 years old, who start earning at about 16 to 22. Anchor: GiveWell's 8 years for school-age children dewormed (@givewell_shared.years_until_income_benefits_deworming), whose pupils are a little younger on average.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: The shared figure (@givewell_shared.long_term_benefit_years), as in every model of later income.

rows.label: Household members who share the earnings gain
rows.explainer: The shared figure (@givewell_shared.resource_sharing_multiplier): the earner's household shares the extra income, as in GiveWell's deworming model.

rows.label: Working years of the gain, discounted to today
rows.explainer: The working years at the discount rate under Your values, after the wait until the pupils start work.

rows.label: Share of the learning that wouldn't have happened without TaRL Africa
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 80% (50% to 100%); the sheet credits TaRL Africa with all of it. The trials' effect is measured against schools without the programme, but the question here is whether the governments would run it, and as well, without TaRL Africa: Pratham, J-PAL and other organisations also help governments run Teaching at the Right Level, and some of the governments' programmes (Zambia's Catch Up among them) might carry on with less support. The scale-up fidelity adjustment above already counts weaker delivery at scale. Anchor: TaRL Africa is the programmes' technical partner in all three countries and no other organisation is named as running them, so most of the credit is its own; we found no count of programmes that carried on after such a partner left, hence the wide range.

rows.label: Good of better learning beyond earnings, as a share of the earnings gain
rows.explainer: A side effect, our judgment 10% (0 to 30%): children who read and count better may also stay in school longer and, as adults, have healthier children; most of that evidence is about years of school rather than test gains, and part of it is already in the earnings figure, so it is counted small. Anchor: a placeholder kept small enough that its whole range moves the result by under a fifth (0% gives 0.91 of the result, 30% gives 1.18).

rows.label: Full cost counted per dollar of TaRL Africa's own (the governments' money leaves the cost)
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The governments that run the programme in their schools carry out the work only because of the charity, so they are credited through the share below (mobiliser_share), not by counting their money in the cost (docs/normalization.md 2.24): counted in both, they would be cut twice. The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's cost (1). TaRL Africa's own cost keeps its central costs and, with credit by share of resources on, its staff's forgone pay.

rows.label: What the governments' money would otherwise have done, per dollar of the full cost counted, units of value
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The governments' spending on the programme (about two thirds of the sheet's cost), valued at GiveWell's figure for what a dollar a government in its programme countries spends would otherwise have done (@givewell_shared.cf_value_government, about 1.5 times cash), the site's one figure for redirected government money (docs/normalization.md 2.20). A cost of the resources TaRL Africa mobilises: netted from the good before the share that wouldn't have happened without it and before the mobiliser's share. The evaluator view counts the governments' money in the cost instead (0 here).

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.formula: (pupils_per_dollar * ln_gain_per_pupil * pv_factor * resource_sharing_multiplier * $uov_per_ln_consumption * (1 + non_income_gains_share) - gov_cost_value_per_dollar) * counterfactual_adoption * adopter_cost_out * mobiliser_share
rows.explainer: Pupils per dollar × the gain in log earnings each working year × the discounted working years × the household sharing it × the value of a unit of log consumption (Your values), plus the gains beyond earnings, less what the governments' money would otherwise have done; × the share due to TaRL Africa, per dollar of TaRL Africa's own cost (adopter_cost_out), × the charity's share of the good that others carry out (mobiliser_share).
